principles: Fix the false positive without weakening any true positive: byte-identical endpoint content means the validation verdict still applies.
One shared classifier used by both copies so they cannot diverge again (audit finding H1).
Fail-closed on any git error, and never silently mislabel a diff/ENOBUFS failure as an ancestry failure.
Touch only the merge-lineage factor; leave the other eight reuse factors, refresh_stale, and the review floor untouched.
drivers: A byte-equivalent second copy (validationHeadLineage in validation-evidence-admissibility.ts) also hard-throws autopilot_review_submit --deriveBindings via verdict.ts:139, so fixing only the reuse copy is insufficient.
Large main-syncs can exceed Node's 1MiB execFileSync default causing ENOBUFS that the catch swallows and mislabels as not-ancestor (B-f492 precedent in evidence-freshness.ts:134).
Pathnames with spaces or non-ASCII are git-quoted unless -z is used, breaking isStoryMetadataPath matching.

options.name: Fix only validation-evidence-reuse.ts (rev-1 scope)
cons: Audit H1: leaves the byte-equivalent admissibility copy, so autopilot_review_submit --deriveBindings still hard-throws the same false positive in hot-main closeout

options.name: Keep per-commit union, filter each path by git diff --quiet endpoint check
pros: Preserves per-path provenance in the reason strings
cons: O(number-of-paths) extra git subprocess calls for provenance no consumer reads
Still two divergent copies unless also unified

options.name: One shared net-diff merge-lineage classifier used by both copies
pros: Fixes both the reuse and the admissibility/autopilot paths at once
Net endpoint diff naturally excludes merge-re-touched unchanged files while still catching genuine content changes
Single source of truth prevents future divergence
Folds the audit robustness fixes (-z, maxBuffer, empty-means-trusted, split catch) into one place
cons: Adds one new module and refactors two call sites (slightly larger diff)
Loses intra-range change-then-revert visibility (semantically correct: identical endpoints mean identical validated content)

chosen: One shared net-diff merge-lineage classifier used by both copies
rationale: The cross-host audit (Claude CLI + Agy CLI, both SOUND-WITH-CHANGES) proved fixing only the reuse copy is insufficient because the admissibility copy independently hard-throws autopilot. A shared net-diff classifier fixes both paths, prevents future divergence, and centralizes the three audit-required robustness fixes. Content identity between endpoints guarantees the reused verdict is still correct; genuine content changes still refuse reuse, so no security property is relaxed.

preMortem.scenario: The empty-net-diff-means-trusted change lets a stale validation be reused
preMortem.trigger: An implementer reads empty as always-safe and drops other guards
preMortem.mitigation: Empty net diff means the endpoint trees are byte-identical (strictly safer than metadata-only change); the other eight reuse factors (genuine receipt + material/storyFiles/identity hashes) still gate independently. Negative smoke asserts a genuine content change still refuses.

preMortem.scenario: The two copies drift again after this fix
preMortem.trigger: A future edit touches one classifier not the other
preMortem.consequence: The merge false positive re-appears on one path
preMortem.mitigation: Both call sites delegate to one shared exported classifier; the smoke exercises both paths so a divergence fails the suite.

preMortem.scenario: netDiffChangedPaths throws ENOBUFS on a large main-sync and is swallowed
preMortem.trigger: A big main merge produces >1MiB of diff output
preMortem.consequence: Silent fall-back to a spurious re-run (the exact bug, reintroduced)
preMortem.mitigation: Explicit maxBuffer 1GiB mirroring evidence-freshness.ts:134; split the catch so a diff failure surfaces a distinct lineage-diff-failed reason instead of mislabeling as not-ancestor.
